**1 — Scene:** A plate of cooked vegetables with browned potato pieces and a few sausage slices. The soup at the left edge is excluded.

**2 — Vessel:** Rounded-square dinner plate, approximately 25–26 cm across. Using an equivalent circular diameter of **26 cm**, its area is **3.14 × 13² ≈ 531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Cauliflower, orange vegetable chunks (assumed cooked carrot), browned potatoes, and sausage slices. Any cooking oil on the potatoes is included in their energy density; no separate sauce is clearly visible.

| Item | Plate coverage | Area | Typical height | Gross volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |

| Sausage slices | 6% | 32 cm² | 1.0 cm | 32 ml | 1.00 g/ml | 32 g | 320 | 102 kcal |

Coverage totals **82%**, consistent with the visible uncovered rim. Each weight uses only gross volume × bulk density.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **537 g and 357 kcal** is plausible for this mostly vegetable-filled dinner plate. The orange chunks could instead be squash, which would change the estimate only modestly.
